name: Batman
summary: A billionaire who turned grief into the world's greatest detective career. Bruce Wayne patrols Gotham City as Batman, with no powers beyond training, gadgets and sheer stubbornness.
origin: Batman is the ultimate proof that being stubborn can count as a superpower. Bill Finger and Bob Kane introduced him in Detective Comics #27 in 1939, and later that year readers learned why: as a boy, Bruce Wayne watched a mugger shoot his parents, Thomas and Martha, on a Gotham street. Instead of moving on, he poured his fortune and his youth into turning himself into a weapon, training his body, his fighting skills and his detective mind to their limits. Then he dressed as a bat to frighten the criminals he hunts. In most eras he refuses to kill or carry a gun, which makes his war on crime harder and far more interesting. It is still the most famous origin in comics.

storyline.title: The Bat-Man
storyline.beat: Batman first appears in Detective Comics #27. Months later his origin is revealed: young Bruce Wayne watched his parents murdered and vowed to wage war on crime.

storyline.title: Building the world
storyline.beat: Robin, Dick Grayson, joins in 1940, and Batman #1 introduces the Joker and Catwoman.

storyline.title: O'Neil and Adams
storyline.beat: After the campy 1960s TV era, Denny O'Neil and Neal Adams take Batman back to his roots as a dark detective and introduce Ra's al Ghul.

storyline.title: Miller's reinvention
storyline.beat: Frank Miller's The Dark Knight Returns and Batman: Year One set the gritty modern tone for the character.

storyline.title: Readers decide
storyline.beat: DC lets fans vote by phone on whether the second Robin, Jason Todd, should survive. They choose death, and the Joker kills him.

storyline.title: Broken
storyline.beat: The villain Bane breaks Batman's back, and a replacement takes the cowl while Bruce recovers.

storyline.title: Gotham's secret
storyline.beat: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo reveal a centuries-old secret society that has secretly controlled Gotham.

gossip.truth: Bill Finger co-created him and wrote many early stories. DC officially credited Finger as co-creator in 2015.

gossip.text: Kane's first sketch had red tights and stiff bat wings. Finger suggested the cowl, the cape and the grey-and-black colours.
The phone vote to kill Jason Todd was decided by fewer than 100 votes.
In his earliest stories Batman sometimes carried a gun.
Dick Grayson, the first Robin, debuted in Detective Comics #38 (1940).

quiz.q: Which villain broke Batman's back in Knightfall?
Who received official co-creator credit for Batman in 2015?
quiz.why: DC added Bill Finger's credit in 2015.

quiz.q: In which comic did Batman debut?

theme.tagline: No powers, all the gadgets, zero sleep.

timeline.title: The Bat-Man arrives
timeline.note: Detective Comics #27 introduces a grim, cowled vigilante who hunts crooks from the shadows of Gotham.

timeline.title: Enter the Boy Wonder
timeline.note: Detective Comics #38 gives Batman a partner, circus orphan Dick Grayson, and the kid sidekick becomes a staple.

timeline.title: First grin
timeline.note: Batman #1 introduces the Joker, a chalk-faced killer who will be his dark mirror for decades.

timeline.title: Batmania hits TV
timeline.note: Adam West's bright, campy TV series becomes a pop phenomenon and makes the Caped Crusader a household name.

timeline.title: The Dark Knight Returns
timeline.note: Frank Miller drags a fifty-something Bruce back into the cape, and superhero comics suddenly grow up.

timeline.title: A Death in the Family
timeline.note: Fans vote by phone, and the Joker murders second Robin Jason Todd. Bruce carries that guilt for years.

timeline.title: Burton goes gothic
timeline.note: Tim Burton casts Michael Keaton in a moody blockbuster that turns the Bat-symbol into the summer's hottest logo.

timeline.title: Batman Begins
timeline.note: Christopher Nolan reboots the films with Christian Bale, pitting a young Bruce against his mentor Ra's al Ghul.
